summary: The note examines how small businesses are using technology and digital transformation to overcome growth challenges, drawing on expert commentary and local examples. It covers barriers such as skills gaps, cost and cybersecurity, along with tools like e-commerce, social media, CRM and chatbots. It concludes that strategic planning and keeping the human touch are essential, and that emerging technologies like VR, blockchain, IoT and 5G are worth watching.
one_line: Experts and examples show how small businesses use digital tools, training, funding and security while keeping the human touch.
key_facts: Carol Anderson, a small business consultant, says digital transformation is now a necessity and that the pandemic accelerated that reality.
On November 5, 2023, bakery owner Mike Bennett implemented inventory management software that reduced waste by 20% and provided data insights on customer preferences.
A boutique in downtown Chicago launched its online store on October 14, 2023 and saw a 100% increase in sales in the first month thanks to a targeted Instagram campaign.
Sarah Jenkins, an e-commerce specialist, says small businesses can tap into global markets through e-commerce, with social media driving traffic.
Florist Elena Rodriguez introduced digital skills workshops for her staff in late September 2023, improving use of the point-of-sale system, online ordering and social media marketing.
James Walton, a digital skills trainer, says upskilling the existing workforce is key to closing the digital skills gap.
On December 1, 2023, a local hardware store implemented a CRM, per CRM expert Robert Lipton, enabling timely servicing reminders that led to repeat business and loyalty.
An online retailer suffered a data breach in early 2023, which expedited its investments in cybersecurity.
Cybersecurity advisor Linda Yang says defense requires a culture of security awareness coupled with the right tools.
A local crafts store raised funds via a Kickstarter campaign in September 2023 to launch an augmented reality app offering virtual craft classes.
Financial advisor Derek Simmons says grants, loans and crowdfunding can ease the financial burden of digital initiatives.
A family-run restaurant used chatbots for reservations so staff could spend more time with customers face-to-face; Emily Torres argues technology should empower, not replace, the human aspect.
Innovation specialist Peter Franklin suggests watching virtual reality, such as virtual property tours by local real estate agents.
